title: yian.cli.v1
description: The documents yian's --json commands write. A command writes exactly one JSON object and a newline on stdout, and nothing else there, except device sign-in (`auth_event`), which writes JSON lines: one document per line, ending with a `done` line or a line with an `error` key. Every document has "format": "yian.cli.v1". Keys are snake_case. Every key a document lists is always present (null where it allows null). Consumers ignore unknown keys; keys are only added within v1. Codes and enum values are only added within v1; a consumer treats an unknown error code as a generic error and ignores an unknown login method. Message and note text is not part of the contract, nor are the number and order of `config check` errors; codes and fields are. Conformance cases still pin the number and order, so the implementations agree. Numbers use yian's lossless JSON form: a float always has a fraction or an exponent (2.0), an int never does. Exit codes: 0 success; 1 a reported problem, with its document on stdout; 2 a usage error (text on stderr, no document); 130 stopped by SIGINT, or by SIGTERM for device sign-in (no document, or no further line). Any other exit, a crash included (exit 1 with a traceback), has no document; a consumer treats stdout that doesn't parse as an internal error. stderr is free-form.

frame.description: A source location: range is [start_line, start_col, end_line, end_col], 1-based with an exclusive end column. note is left out when empty.

diagnostic.description: A problem with a code, a message and its source frames, outermost first. frames and notes are left out when empty.

failure.description: A diagnostic plus `node`: the id of the node that failed, or null when no single node did.

run_document.description: `yian run --json` (fresh or --resume): the run's terminal result, or `waiting`. A run that fails exits 1 with status failed; a waiting run exits 0.

output.description: The flow's output in yian's JSON codec form (tests/conformance/SPEC.md): plain JSON, a file as {uri, mime, name}, a float infinity as {"$float": "inf"} or {"$float": "-inf"}, and a mapping that would read as one of those or whose only key is $record wrapped in {"$record": ...}.

waits.description: The calls the run waits on, by waiting node in the order it started waiting.

wake_at.description: The earliest deadline of a call not yet settled, or null when none has one.

error_document.description: Written by a --json command that exits 1 without its own result document.

input.description: One declared flow input. type is the canonical type label (int, Optional(str), a typedef expanded as {"age":int,"name":str}).

flow_result.description: One flow `yian check` loaded; path is the argument exactly as given.

check_document.description: `yian check --json`: one result per flow argument, in argument order.

config_error.description: One problem with an llm_config layer. field is the location joined with `.` (base_url, openai.temperature), or null for an unknown top-level key, which is never named, or a problem with no single field. A provider block reports its own field problems, an unknown key in it included, at field: <block> (openai).

config_document.description: `yian config check --json`: the llm_config layer on stdin, checked as a run checks it. ok is true exactly when errors is empty. Values never appear in messages; an unknown top-level key is never named, but a provider block's messages name its own keys.

provider.description: One supported provider: the login kinds `yian auth` can save for it, and the environment variable its API key is read from (null when it takes no key).

providers_document.description: `yian providers --json`: every supported provider, in yian's order.

skill_result.description: One skill directory `yian skills check` loaded; path is the argument exactly as given.

skills_document.description: `yian skills check --json`: one result per skill directory argument, in argument order. Two directories with one skill name are not reported.

remove_document.description: `yian auth --remove --auth-file F --json` and `yian auth PROVIDER --remove --json`: the whole auth file, or the provider's saved login, is removed. Removing an auth file that doesn't exist succeeds; removing a provider login that isn't saved is an auth.failed error.

auth_event.description: One line of `yian auth openai --method subscription --login device --json`: `code` (enter user_code at verification_uri), then `waiting` at once, before the first poll, then `done` once the login is saved, or `error`. done.models lists the subscription's models in its order; done.model is the one saved: --model when given, else the first. An error before the code is the only line. Exit 0 after done, 1 after error, 130 when SIGTERM or SIGINT stops the sign-in, after which no line follows and nothing is saved.

models_document.description: `yian models --json`: the models the openai subscription login in --auth-file offers, in its order, or the model ids the --provider's host lists, sorted; null when the provider has no model listing (azure).

status_document.description: `yian status LOG --json` (TS only): where the run in the log stands, read without appending or taking the writer's lock. status is running while a writer holds the log's lock; succeeded, failed or cancelled once the run ended; waiting when its last segment ended with every unsettled node waiting (on a take, a sleep or a host call); stopped when the host stopped its last segment; else crashed (the process ended mid-run). in_flight lists the nodes started (or woken) and neither settled nor waiting, in start order (empty for an ended run). crashed_attempts maps a node id to the attempts a resume retried, or would retry, after a crash.

ready.description: For a waiting run, whether some waiting node can be woken now (every call it waits on is settled); false otherwise. A host also wakes the run once wake_at is due.

wake_at.description: For a waiting run, the earliest deadline of an open call of a waiting node, as a UTC time such as 2026-10-20T14:02:11.123Z; null when none has one, and for any other status.

run_status.description: Where a run stands, as `yian status` reads it.

runs_document.description: `yian status --json` with no LOG (TS only): the runs in ~/.yian/runs from the run index, oldest first. Each run's status, ready and wake_at read as `yian status LOG` reads them.

started_at.description: Null when the log's first record can't be read.

memories.description: The memories the run was bound to, as its START inputs recorded them, by input name; an Optional memory left out isn't listed. Identities only, never a location.

last_seq.description: Null when no record could be read.

result.description: The run's output once it succeeded, else null.

unreadable.description: For a log yian can't read, the seq of the first record it couldn't read and why, else null. The other fields hold the records before it.
